name: Ichimoku cloud (kumo breakout and TK cross)

origin.source_title: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo books, commonly dated to 1969 (date as usually cited, not verified)

how_it_works.simple: Draw a shaded 'cloud' from averages of past highs and lows. Price above the cloud means up-trend, so buy; below means down-trend, so sell.
how_it_works.analogy: Like reading weather from a cloud bank: you only go out sailing when the sky above you is clear of it.
how_it_works.precise: Ichimoku uses midpoints of high-low ranges: Tenkan (9), Kijun (26), Senkou A ((Tenkan+Kijun)/2 shifted 26 ahead), Senkou B (52-period midpoint shifted 26 ahead); the space between A and B is the cloud. Retail rules buy when price closes above the cloud and Tenkan crosses above Kijun. Lim, Yanyali and Savidge (2016) argue it behaves like a momentum and breakout strategy with a natural stop loss.

rule: Daily: long when close > max(Senkou A, Senkou B) and Tenkan(9) > Kijun(26); short when close < min(Senkou A, Senkou B) and Tenkan < Kijun; exit when price closes back inside the cloud.
data_needed: Daily high, low and close (FX OHLC from a free source such as Yahoo or Stooq; FRED gives closes only)
economic_rationale: Same trend logic as breakouts. Lim, Yanyali and Savidge (2016) say returns are positively skewed with a small left tail because of the built-in stop.
why_it_might_fail: The only test we found is on single stocks in Japan and the US over 2005 to 2014, and we could only read the abstract. The 9/26/52 settings come from a six-day trading week and were never tuned out of sample.

reported_results.source: Lim, Yanyali and Savidge (2016), Do Ichimoku cloud charts work and do they work better in Japan?, abstract
reported_results.market: Single stocks in Japan and the USA
reported_results.notes: Abstract read through its OpenAlex record (SSRN page blocked to our fetcher). Long-only and short-only conservative and aggressive variants; the abstract gives no return numbers.

implementations.notes: Pure pandas indicator library, includes Ichimoku, Donchian channel, Bollinger, RSI, MACD.
Event-driven backtester with built-in indicators and order types (stops, OCO).

relevance.reason: Testable on daily FX with free OHLC data, but it is mostly a repackaged breakout rule with little independent evidence.
